concepts.title: The Questions of Philosophy: Universe, Self and the Creator
concepts.definition: Philosophy begins in wonder: looking at the earth, moon, stars, mountains and the cycle of birth and death, human beings ask who created these and who controls them. Indian philosophical discourse names its central concerns metaphysical -- atman (the self), srishti (the universe) and the nature of ultimate reality.
concepts.key_idea: Wonder is the first philosopher -- questions about the universe, the self and their source open all Indian thought.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks102.txt opening sections (wonder at creation, metaphysical concepts atman srishti, nature of self, philosophical discourse)

why is philosophy said to begin in wonder
list the metaphysical concerns of indian philosophy

solution_steps.explain: The chapter opens with the seen world -- skies, seasons, life and death -- provoking the question of its source and control.
The questioning matures into metaphysics: atman, srishti, and the relation of self to ultimate reality.
Sustained discourse on these questions crystallised into India's philosophical schools.

concepts.title: The Vedic Roots and Schools of Indian Philosophy
concepts.definition: Indian philosophical schools grew from Vedic discourse and diversified into parallel traditions -- systems that accept Vedic authority and those that do not, debating matter, consciousness, knowledge and liberation. The chapter presents this plurality as reasoned argument rather than fixed dogma.
concepts.key_idea: One Vedic root, many branches -- Indian philosophy is a family of argued schools, not a single creed.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks102.txt school sections (vedas, orthodox and heterodox schools, debate traditions, schools of indian philosophy)
question_patterns: name the major schools of indian philosophy

how did the vedas influence indian philosophical traditions
why is debate central to indian philosophy

what questions do the schools share despite differences

solution_steps.explain: The Vedas supply the earliest layer of reflection on reality, duty and liberation.
Accepting or rejecting Vedic authority, schools arise -- each a coherent answer-set to the shared questions.
Schools argued with one another publicly, so philosophy advanced as dialogue, not decree.

concepts.title: Philosophy as a Way of Living
concepts.definition: Indian philosophy never stayed academic: each system carried ethical consequences for daily living -- duties, self-discipline and paths toward liberation. Its questions about knowledge, right action and the self aimed at a life examined and transformed, not merely a worldview admired.
concepts.key_idea: Philosophy here is practice -- every school is also a discipline for living, not just a theory.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks102.txt living sections (ethics, duties, paths of liberation, discipline, philosophy in daily life)
question_patterns: how does indian philosophy guide daily living
in class 11 philosophy chapter: what is meant by liberation as a goal

why is self discipline stressed in indian traditions
what duties flow from philosophical understanding
show how knowledge and action join in indian thought

solution_steps.explain: Each view of the self and world implies duties -- how to act, what to renounce.
The systems share a horizon of freedom from bondage, reached through knowledge, action or devotion.
Disciplines of conduct turn doctrine into daily practice -- the test of philosophy is the changed life.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The chapter opens with the starry sky and the cycle of life and death. Explain how such observation matures into metaphysics.

solution_template.explain: Observation first asks simple questions: who made this, who controls it?
Sustained questioning names its objects -- atman for the self, srishti for the universe.
When answers are argued systematically, metaphysics -- and philosophy -- has begun.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A friend says philosophy is useless book-talk. Use the chapter's view of philosophy as a way of living to answer.

solution_template.explain: Yes, philosophy argues about self and universe -- but that is only half.
Each school prescribes disciplines: duties, self-control, paths toward liberation.
In India philosophy is tested in living; done rightly, it changes the philosopher, not just the bookshelf.
